findings.claim: A single retain_for_request failure now aborts the entire runner loop via `?`, permanently halting processing of all queued runs.
findings.evidence: Hunk @@ -200,7 +200,13 @@: `for record in &records { if !record.state.is_terminal() { artifacts.retain_for_request(&record.request)?; } }` — the `?` propagates out of `runner_loop`, which previously only failed on `records()?`. One record referencing a missing/corrupt artifact hash (e.g. after a crash between submit and retain, or a partially collected store) kills the daemon's execution path for every other run.
findings.suggested_fix: Log the error and `continue` to the next record (or skip the record and mark it failed) instead of propagating; only ledger-level failures should abort the loop.

findings.claim: retain_for_receipt is called before commit_terminal, so a commit failure leaks receipt pins that the pin-aware GC will never reclaim.
findings.evidence: Hunk @@ -386,12 +392,14 @@: `artifacts.retain_for_receipt(&claim.record.request, &receipt)?;` precedes `service.commit_terminal(...)?`. If commit_terminal fails (ledger I/O, hash conflict), the function returns early — `garbage_collect()` is skipped and the receipt pins remain with no corresponding terminal ledger record to trigger their release. Per criterion 1.3 ('pin-aware budget enforcement'), pinned artifacts are exempt from collection, so repeated failures permanently consume the artifact budget.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap commit in a scope that unpins the receipt pins on failure, or move pin acquisition/release into a transactional helper that rolls back if commit_terminal errors.

findings.claim: Pins created by put_pinned in run_command are never released on error paths, permanently leaking pinned artifacts exempt from garbage collection.
findings.evidence: Hunk @@ -265,8 +265,10 @@: `artifacts.put_pinned(&code, &request_pin)?` then, per input, `artifacts.put_pinned(&fs::read(path)?, &request_pin)?`. If any later input fails to parse (the `ok_or_else`/empty-name checks) or `fs::read` fails, the function returns Err with the code blob and earlier inputs still pinned under `request:{request_id}`. Nothing in the diff unpins on this failure path, and if the subsequent submit fails (e.g. same-hash conflict from criterion 3.1) the request never reaches a terminal state, so the request pin is never released either.
findings.suggested_fix: On any error after the first put_pinned, call an unpin/release for `request_pin` before returning, or stage all inputs in memory first and only pin once validation succeeds, with a cleanup guard on submit failure.

findings.claim: retain_for_request runs before service.submit, so failed submits and replays of terminal requests add request pins with no release path.
findings.evidence: Hunk @@ -281,6 +281,14 @@: `artifacts.retain_for_request(&request)` executes, then `match service.submit(request)`. If submit errors (hash conflict, validation failure), the handler returns the error but the pin remains. For a replayed request (`result.replayed` branch) whose run is already terminal, the request is re-pinned after the terminal commit/GC cycle may already have released its request pins, re-protecting artifacts the lifecycle expects to be collectable.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip retain_for_request when submit returns a replayed/conflict result (retain only on accepted new submissions), and unpin on submit error paths.

findings.claim: synthetic_receipt calls garbage_collect before its returned receipt is committed by the caller, making the GC pass ineffective for this request and leaking pins if the later commit fails.
findings.evidence: Hunk @@ -491,6 +499,8 @@: `artifacts.retain_for_receipt(&record.request, &receipt)?; artifacts.garbage_collect()?; Ok(receipt)` — the receipt is returned to the caller, so commit_terminal happens after this function returns. At GC time the record is not yet terminal, so this request's pins are all still active and cannot be reclaimed; conversely if the caller's commit subsequently fails, both the request and receipt pins leak with no cleanup.
findings.suggested_fix: Move retain_for_receipt + garbage_collect to after the caller's commit_terminal (mirroring the intended ordering in process_queued_run), or document and handle the commit-failure unpin path.
